definition-dropped.flag: character | in a coded character set (newer: undefined); character | in a screen item (newer: undefined); character | in cobol character repertoire (newer: undefined); character | in computer storage (newer: undefined); national character (newer: undefined); type | for type declaration (newer: 8.5.3)
definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 defines 'character' in four senses (in a coded character set, in a screen item, in the COBOL character repertoire, in computer storage) and 'coded character set' as "A set of unambiguous rules that establishes a character set" (taken from ISO/IEC 10646-1); 2023 drops these entries and takes the terms from its normative reference ISO/IEC 10646 (§2023:2), in the same sense. RV2 counts 'national character positions'. 'national character' (§2002:4: "A character in a national character set") is the same notion 2023 uses with its kept 'national character set' entry (§2023:3.125); this compiler's national set is UTF-16 in both editions. 'type (for type declaration)' is defined in §2002:4 in the words 2023 keeps (3.174) and §2002:8.5.3 repeats; the type-declaration case is covered (p4_length.cob TN 4).

pending-clause.answer: §2002:8.5.3 defines a type as in 2023; §2002:8.5.4 makes a group holding only a zero-occurrence ODO item a zero-length item, which RV2 then measures as 0: probed now at --std 2002, a GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL group with OCCURS 0 TO 5 DEPENDING ON CNT gives LENGTH 0 at CNT=0 and 6 at CNT=3 (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out-answer/probes-a-15/len_nat_zero-results.txt). The result is an integer count, so standard arithmetic (§2002:8.8.1.x) and alignment (§2002:14.5.8) are not involved; §2002:15/15.1's differing text does not bear on it (§2002:15.39 "The type of this function is integer").
